positions.subject: q:education/sfusd-proximity-assignment
positions.summary: KQED reports that Tello believes families want neighborhood schools when a strong school is nearby, that the overhaul should bring resources and programs closer to families, and that students whose needs cannot be met nearby should be able to enroll elsewhere.

citations.quote: Tello believes that families want to send their kids to schools in their neighborhoods if there is a “great” school close by.
citations.locator: Positions on Key Issues, student-assignment question

citations.quote: Students who have special needs that can’t be met at their neighborhood school, she says, should be allowed to enroll elsewhere.
citations.locator: Positions on Key Issues, student-assignment question

positions.subject: q:education/sfusd-spend-reserves
positions.summary: Tello says SFUSD should spend its reserves down to a level closer to the state-required 2% so current funds go to current students.

citations.quote: We need to spend these down to a reasonable level—closer to the state-required 2%—to ensure today’s dollars are spent on today’s students
